title: SAT Lines, Angles & Triangles: Parallel Lines and Similar Triangles
description:
SAT lines, angles, and triangles questions come down to three things: which angles are equal, which ones add up to 180°, and which triangles are the same shape. This lesson covers every rule you need, the traps that cost the most points, and 6 SAT-style practice questions.

You'll learn:
• Vertical angles and linear pairs
• Parallel lines cut by a transversal: corresponding, alternate interior, and same-side interior angles
• Triangle angle sum and the exterior angle theorem
• Isosceles and equilateral triangles
• Similar triangles, including a triangle split by a segment parallel to one side
• Congruence basics: what's sufficient and what isn't
• A 5-step test-day method

All questions are original SAT-style questions written for this video, not official College Board questions. For official practice, use the free SAT Suite Question Bank (Geometry and Trigonometry → Lines, angles, and triangles).
